ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p424/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p424/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p424/r1.claim: The oath by earlier scriptures and the Qur’an completes the claim that Muhammad is not possessed but teaches the same message as prophets from Adam to Jesus, whose truth history confirms.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p424/r1.anchor: he is, in fact, imparting to people the same teachings as were imparted by all other prophets of God from Adam (sws) to Jesus (sws)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p424/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p424/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p424/r2.claim: Quraysh called Muhammad mad because they could not understand his certainty about impending punishment and saw his anxious, compassionate preaching influencing people; they alleged hallucination and magic to discredit him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p424/r2.anchor: their leaders were totally unable to understand from where the punishment with which he was emphatically and vehemently warning them

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.claim: Most of the sūra was revealed concerning al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and Abū Jahl; its opening refutes accusations of madness and praises the Prophet's patience and character.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.anchor: ومعظمها نزل في الوليد بن المغيرة وأبي جهل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.claim: The sūra follows a prior account of the blessed and wretched and God's power and knowledge, answering claims that the Prophet's revelation was poetry, magic, or madness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.anchor: وكان الكفار ينسبونه مرة إلى الشعر، ومرة إلى السحر، ومرة إلى الجنون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r10.claim: Those who identify N with the cosmic fish take the pen as the divinely created pen recording decrees and “they write” as angels; those who take N as a name identify the familiar pen and human writers, citing Ibn ʿAbbās.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r10.anchor: فمن جعله البهموت، جعل القلم هو الذي خلقه الله وأمره بكتب الكائنات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r11.claim: The oath presents writing as a foundation of knowledge and worldly and otherworldly affairs; the pen is a universal divine blessing and companion to speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r11.anchor: فإن القلم أخو اللسان ونعمة من الله عامة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r14.claim: ما may be relative or a verbal noun; the pronoun in “they write” may refer to the written book signaled by the pen, meaning recording angels or every writer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r14.anchor: وما يحتمل أن تكون موصولة ومصدرية، والضمير في يسطرون عائد على الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r15.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the pen may mean its users, so “they write” refers to those people and their written pages or act of writing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r15.anchor: ويجوز أن يراد بالقلم أصحابه، فيكون الضمير في يسطرون لهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r1.claim: The oath's answer is the declaration that the Prophet is not mad; “by your Lord's favor” is an emphatic parenthesis between subject and predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r1.anchor: ويظهر أن بنعمة ربك قسم اعترض به بين المحكوم عليه والحكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls “by your Lord's favor” a parenthesis but does not say what the preposition attaches to.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: بنعمة ربك اعتراض، كما تقول للإنسان: أنت بحمد الله فاضل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attaches the phrase to “mad” as a circumstantial phrase: by God's favor, the Prophet is not mad; the extra preposition reinforces negation and signals fitness for prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r3.anchor: يتعلق بمجنون منفيا، كما يتعلق بعاقل مثبتا في قولك: أنت بنعمة الله عاقل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says this attachment requires scrutiny: negation can scope over the predicate alone or over predicate and adjunct, and the latter reading yields an impermissible implication about the infallible Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r4.anchor: وما ذهب إليه الزمخشري من أن بنعمة ربك متعلق بمجنون، وأنه في موضع الحال، يحتاج إلى تأمل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r5.claim: Another interpretation reads the clause as “you are not mad, and the favor is from your Lord”; this is a semantic gloss rather than a syntactic parse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r5.anchor: أي والحمد لله، ومنه قول لبيد:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r6.claim: A summary of al-Muntakhab says God's favor removed a blameworthy trait and supplied a praiseworthy one; the Prophet's eloquence, reason, sound character, and virtue demonstrate that his accusers lie.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r6.anchor: وفي المنتخب ما ملخصه المعنى: انتفى عنك الجنون بنعمة ربك،

TABATABAI:68:1-33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r1.claim: The Prophet is not mad because of his Lord's favor; the context identifies that favor as prophethood, whose proof excludes mental disorder needed to undermine divine guidance.
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r1.anchor: والسياق يؤيد أن المراد بهذه النعمة النبوة فإن دليل النبوة يدفع عن النبي كل اختلال عقلي

TABATABAI:68:1-33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r2.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r2.claim: Another view identifies the favor as the Prophet's eloquence, complete reason, good conduct, freedom from defects, and possession of virtues; the author says prophethood is a more decisive proof.
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد بالنعمة فصاحته صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

TABATABAI:68:1-33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r3.claim: The verse and what follows comfort and support the Prophet while refuting the accusation repeated at the surah's end.

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that Quraysh insulted ʿAli after the Prophet honored him; the passage identifies the slanderers as those astray and ʿAli as among the guided.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك قال لما رأت قريش تقديم النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عليا وإعظامه له نالوا من علي

TABRISI:68:1-16/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16/r4.claim: One parse treats المفتون as a verbal noun meaning trial or temptation, as in expressions using معقول and محصول for a thing's rationality or outcome.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r4.anchor: أن المفتون مصدر بمعنى الفتنة كما يقال ليس له معقول وما له محصول

TABRISI:68:1-16/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16/r5.claim: A second parse treats المفتون as a passive participle, with an extra باء; the sense is 'which of you is the afflicted one,' and the clause depends on يبصرون.
TABRISI:68:1-16/r5.anchor: وثانيها: أن يكون المفتون اسم المفعول والباء مزيدة والتقدير أيكم المفتون

TABRISI:68:1-16/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16/r6.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:68:1-16/r6.claim: Al-Farra takes باء as meaning 'in': which group contains the madman, the Muslims or disbelievers; a rajaz line supports using an extra باء for 'we hope for relief.'
TABRISI:68:1-16/r6.anchor: وثالثها: أن الباء بمعنى في المعنى في أيكم المفتون أي في أي الفريقين في فرقة الإسلام أو في فرقة الكفر المجنون وهذا قول الفراء

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r4.claim: The oath's answer denies that Muhammad is mad by his Lord's grace; the fronted complement uses an emphatic extra bāʾ.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r4.anchor: هو جواب القسم ومعناه لست يا محمد بمجنون بنعمة ربك كما تقول ما أنت بنعمة ربك بجاهل

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r5.claim: The construction is estimated as madness having been removed from him by God's grace.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r5.anchor: وجاز تقديم معمولها به الباء لأنها زائدة مؤكدة وتقديره انتفى عنك الجنون بنعمة ربك

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r6.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r6.claim: The phrase means simply that he is not mad, praise be to God.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو كما يقال ما أنت بمجنون بحمد الله

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r7.claim: God's gifts of full intellect, prophethood, and wisdom are incompatible with madness.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: معناه بما أنعم عليك ربك من كمال العقل والنبوة والحكمة لست بمجنون

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r8.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, he is not mad, and grace belongs to the Lord, like the phrase “praise belongs to You.”
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: معناه ما أنت بمجنون والنعمة لربك كما يقال سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك

RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r7.claim: After mentioning the objects of the oath, God states what is sworn: the Prophet is not mad, will have an undiminished reward, and has exalted character.
RAZI-FULL:v30p69#3/r7.anchor: لما ذكر المقسم به أتبعه بذكر المقسم عليه

RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās relates that the Prophet went to Ḥirāʾ and Khadīja searched for him; he told her Gabriel brought the first revelation, taught him ablution and prayer, and she consulted her Christian cousin Waraqa, who promised support but died before the call; Quraysh then called the Prophet mad.
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه عليه السلام غاب عن خديجة

RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r2.claim: Rāzī says God swore the Prophet was not mad in response to the Quraysh accusation, and identifies this as the first five verses of the sūra.
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r2.anchor: فأقسم الله تعالى على أنه ليس بمجنون

RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says the first revelation was “Glorify the name of your Lord Most High,” making this verse the second revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r3.anchor: وأول ما نزل قوله : { سبح اسم ربك }

RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj parses anta as the subject noun of mā and bimajnūn as its predicate; biniʿmati rabbik is parenthetical.
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج : { أنت } هو اسم { ما }

RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r5.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains the phrase as saying that madness is absent through God’s grace, as in expressions that attribute intelligence or freedom from poverty to God’s blessing.

RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r6.speaker: عطاء وابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and Ibn ʿAbbās say the blessing means the faith and prophethood bestowed on the Messenger, answering those who called him mad.
RAZI-FULL:v30p70/r6.anchor: وقال عطاء وابن عباس : يريد بنعمة ربك عليك بالإيمان والنبوة

RAZI-FULL:v30p70#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p70#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p70#2/r1.claim: God’s visible gifts to the Prophet—eloquence, complete intellect, commendable conduct, freedom from defects, and possession of virtues—are incompatible with madness and expose the accusers as liars.
RAZI-FULL:v30p70#2/r1.anchor: نعم الله تعالى كانت ظاهرة في حقه من الفصاحة التامة والعقل الكامل والسيرة المرضية

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r1.claim: The denial of madness explains the preceding reference to God’s favor and calls the accusation false.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r1.anchor: اعلم أن هذا كالتفسير لما تقدم

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r2.claim: The Prophet’s visible excellent morals and actions are incompatible with the bad morals characteristic of madmen.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r2.anchor: الأخلاق الحميدة والأفعال المرضية كانت ظاهرة منه

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r3.claim: His conduct was not affectation: as 38:86 says, he did not pretend, and pretense soon gives way to one’s natural disposition.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r3.anchor: لست متكلفا فيما يظهر لكم من أخلاقي لأن المتكلف لا يدوم أمره طويلا بل يرجع إلى الطبع

STUDYQURAN:68:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:2/r1.claim: The blessing of the Lord may refer to the Prophet’s prophethood.
STUDYQURAN:68:2/r1.anchor: The blessing of thy Lord may be a reference to prophethood

STUDYQURAN:68:2/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:2/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:2/r2.claim: The denial that the Prophet is possessed directly answers the disbelievers’ charge in 15:6–7.
STUDYQURAN:68:2/r2.anchor: verse’s assertion that the Prophet is not possessed can be seen as a direct response to the derogatory statement of the disbelievers in 15:6–7

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r11.claim: Beautiful character can be understood as the opposite of the state of being possessed mentioned in verse 2.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r11.anchor: those with beautiful character traits are far from the state of being possessed referred to in verse 2 (Āl)

BURSEVI:v10p80/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r1.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p80/r1.claim: Al-Qashani reads nūn as the universal soul and the Pen as the universal intellect; the first is alluded to by its initial letter, the second likened to a pen inscribing forms in a tablet.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r1.anchor: ن هو النفس الكلية والقلم هو العقل الكلي والأول من باب الكناية بالاكتفاء من الكلمة

BURSEVI:v10p80/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r2.speaker: القاشاني
BURSEVI:v10p80/r2.claim: What is written comprises forms, configurations, and destined states of things; intermediate intellects and holy spirits are its scribes, though God is the true writer and their agency is metaphorically attributed in the realm of the Divine Names.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r2.anchor: وما يسطرون من صور الأشياء وما هيأتها وأحوالها المقدرة على ما تقع عليه

BURSEVI:v10p80/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p80/r3.claim: The oath by the Pen, the soul, and what they write suits the sworn statement because these are noble, encompass existence at the first level of influence, and are principles of existence and divine determination.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r3.anchor: لشرفهما وكونما مشتملين على كل الوجود في أول مرتبة التأثير والتأثر

BURSEVI:v10p80/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p80/r4.claim: The bāʾ in bi-niʿmati is attached to an omitted circumstantial expression describing the pronoun in the predicate majnūn; its governor is the sense of negation.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r4.anchor: والباء متعلقة بمضمر هو حال من الضمير في خبر ما وهو مجنون

BURSEVI:v10p80/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p80/r5.claim: Madness is a barrier between soul and intellect; the word may describe being struck by jinn or the heart, or having soul and intellect separated.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r5.anchor: والجنون حائل بين النفس والعقل وجن فلان أي أصابه الجن أوأصاب جنانه

BURSEVI:v10p80/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p80/r6.claim: The Prophet is entirely free of the madness charged against him by hostile, envious deniers; by God's favor he is endowed with prophethood and general leadership.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r6.anchor: أنت بريء منه ملتبسا بنعمة الله التي هي النبوة والرياسة العامة

BURSEVI:v10p80/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r7.speaker: أبو حيان
BURSEVI:v10p80/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls the phrase an oath interposed between subject and predicate to intensify the denial of the Prophet's vile alleged trait.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r7.anchor: قال أبو حيان قوله : بنعمة ربك قسم اعترض به بين المحكوم عليه والحكم

BURSEVI:v10p80/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r8.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v10p80/r8.claim: Najm al-Dīn also treats the phrase as an oath in his Taʾwīlāt.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r8.anchor: حضرة الشيخ نجم الدين في تأويلاته روى

BURSEVI:v10p80/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p80/r9.claim: A report recounts the Prophet's first revelation at Ḥirāʾ, Gabriel teaching him prayer, Khadīja consulting Waraqa, and Quraysh later calling him mad; God swore he was not mad. The passage says the sūra's first five verses were among the earliest revealed.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r9.anchor: غاب عن خديجة رضي الله عنها إلى حراء فلم تجده فإذا هو قد طلع

BURSEVI:v10p80/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p80/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the first revelation was the command to glorify the Lord, and this verse was the second.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r10.anchor: أول ما نزل قوله سبح اسم ربك وهذه الآية هي الثانية

BURSEVI:v10p80/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p80/r11.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v10p80/r11.claim: In the Najmiyya reading, the Prophet is not veiled from what was eternally past or will be eternally future: jinn means concealment, while his knowledge encompasses both; the excerpt begins citing a gesture as evidence.
BURSEVI:v10p80/r11.anchor: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمستور عما كان من الأزل وما سيكون إلى الأبد

THALABI:v10p8/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p8/r6.claim: The Prophet is not mad; by God's favor He bestowed prophecy upon him.
THALABI:v10p8/r6.anchor: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون يعني أنك لا تكون مجنونا وقد أنعم الله عليك بالنبوة

THALABI:v10p8/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r7.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p8/r7.claim: Another gloss takes the phrase as “by the protection of your Lord.”

THALABI:v10p8/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r8.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p8/r8.claim: One construction reads the sense as “you are not mad, praise be to God,” with an omitted expression of praise.
THALABI:v10p8/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو كما يقال: ما أنت بمجنون والحمد لله

THALABI:v10p8/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r9.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p8/r9.claim: Another construction supplies an omitted conjunction: “you are not mad, and the favor belongs to your Lord,” like the formula “Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You.”
THALABI:v10p8/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه ما أنت بمجنون والنعمة لربك كقولهم: سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك

THALABI:v10p8/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r10.speaker: لبيد
THALABI:v10p8/r10.claim: Labid's line supplies an omitted “and he is” in “by Arbad,” illustrating the proposed ellipsis.
THALABI:v10p8/r10.anchor: وقال لبيد: وأفردت في الدنيا بفقد عشيرتي … وفارقني جار بأربد نافع

THALABI:v10p8/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r11.speaker: النابغة
THALABI:v10p8/r11.claim: Al-Nabigha's line likewise supplies an understood omitted conjunction before “Natiq.”
THALABI:v10p8/r11.anchor: وقال النابغة: لم يحرموا حسن الغداء وأمهم … طفحت عليك بناتق مذكار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74/r1.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74/r1.claim: Abū Isḥāq parses anta as the noun of mā, bimajnūn as its predicate, and bi-naʿmati rabbika as attached to the negation: by your Lord’s favor, madness is denied of you.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r1.claim: The verse answers the accusation in 15:6 that the recipient of the Reminder is mad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r1.anchor: وهذا جواب لقوله: {يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r2.claim: Muqātil says the Meccan unbelievers called Muḥammad mad, so God swore by the whale, pen, and human deeds; “by your Lord’s favor” means by His mercy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل: وذلك حين قال كفار مكة: إن محمدا مجنون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r3.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r3.claim: ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās says the blessing is God’s gift of faith and prophethood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p74#3/r3.anchor: وقال عطاء عن (¬5) ابن عباس: يريد بنعمة ربك عليك بالإيمان والنبوة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r4.claim: God’s favor here is His granting Muhammad prophethood, which rules out the accusation that he is mad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r4.anchor: أي: إنك لا تكون مجنونا وقد أنعم الله عليك بالنبوة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r5.claim: The verse answers the opponents’ claim that the recipient of the Reminder is mad.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:1-3/r5.anchor: وهذا جواب لقولهم: وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون

QASHANI:68:2-4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:2-4/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:2-4/r1.claim: By his Lord's gift of insight into what the Soul and Intellect inscribe, the Prophet is not mentally veiled or deficient; one who sees destiny's secret and realities as they are is supremely rational.
QASHANI:68:2-4/r1.anchor: ما أنت بمستور العقل مختل الإدراك في حالة كونك منعما عليك بنعمة الاطلاع

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.claim: The following denial of madness, affirmation of divine favor, understanding, character, and great reward, and condemnation of immoral liars clarify which side of the pen’s significance is praised.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.anchor: Bundan dolayı burada bu kasemin arkasından cünûnun, fitnenin nefyi ve ni‘met-i rabbâniyenin idrak ve ahlâkın, ecrin büyüklüğünü beyan ve ahlâksızların, yalancıların zemmi ile o cihete de tenbih buyurulacaktır

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r1.claim: The denial and its coordinated clauses answer the preceding oath.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r2.speaker: Ebû Hayyân
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r2.claim: Abu Hayyan takes bi as an oath particle in a parenthetical clause, strengthening the negation.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r2.anchor: Ebû Hayyân nefiyde daha ziyade kuvvet ifade etmek üzere cümle-i mu‘teriza hâlinde kasem için olmasını zâhir görmüştür

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r3.speaker: İbn Atıyye
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r3.claim: Ibn Atiyya treats the phrase as a parenthetical like bihamdillah: by God's praise, you possess virtue.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r4.speaker: Zemahşerî
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r4.claim: Zamakhshari attaches bi to the negated predicate: by God's favor the Prophet is rational, with that favor underlying both the denial of madness and affirmation of reason.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r4.anchor: Zemahşerî ise menfî olan habere ta‘allukuyla

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r5.speaker: Zemahşerî
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r5.claim: Alternatively, Zamakhshari construes the phrase as a stable adverbial state from anta.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r5.anchor: zarf-ı müstekar olarak أَنتَ’den hâl olmasını söylemiştir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r6.claim: God's favor means prophethood and its prerequisites: intellect, discernment, good character, virtue, and gifts that bring worldly and afterlife felicity.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r6.anchor: nübüvvet ve levâzımı olan akıl ve şehâmet ve hüsn-i ahlâk

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r7.claim: At the start of revelation, Meccan opponents out of envy, hostility, and confusion falsely accused Muhammad of madness and error; he is instead distinguished by reason, uprightness, and virtue bestowed by God for his mission.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r7.anchor: Mekke küffârının hased ve adavet ve şaşkınlıkla nisbet etmeye kalkıştıkları mecnunluk ve sapıklık şâibelerinin kendisinden uzak, bilakis onun akl ü şehâmet

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r2.claim: Meccan polytheists believed poets, soothsayers, and magicians received inspiration from jinn, and accused Muhammad of being similarly influenced and mad.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r2.anchor: Hz. Peygamber’in de onlar gibi cinlerin etkisi altına girdiğine ve söylediklerinin ona cinler tarafından telkin edildiğine inandıkları için

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r3.claim: In response, God swears by the pen and writers' lines to deny that the Prophet is mad and affirm his divine favor, namely the honor of prophethood.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r3.anchor: Allah Teâlâ kaleme ve kalem ehlinin yazdığı satırlara yemin ederek onun, iddia edildiği gibi mecnun olmadığını

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r15.claim: Together these verses present the Prophet as divinely favored, exemplary in character, a model leader for humanity, and a trustworthy guide, contrary to the polytheists' charge of madness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r15.anchor: Allah’ın lutfuna mazhar olmuş yüksek bir şahsiyete ve üstün bir ahlâka sahip, her yönüyle mükemmel

BAQILLANI:v1p96/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r1.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r1.claim: Bāqillānī presents the verses as Qur’anic examples of tarsīʿ combined with tajnīs, alongside other balanced endings and phrases.
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r1.anchor: ومن ذلك الترصيع مع التجنيس كقول ابن المعتز

BAQILLANI:v1p96/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r2.claim: He offers Imruʾ al-Qays and Abu Nuwas poems among examples of the ornament discussed in the passage, and says poets use tarsīʿ either at points or throughout a poem, as Ibn al-Rumi does.
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r2.anchor: وقد أولع الشعراء بنحو هذا فأكثروا فيه ومنهم من اقتنع بالترصيع في بعض أطراف الكلام ومنهم من بنى كلامه كله عليه كقول ابن الرومي

BAQILLANI:v1p96/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r3.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r3.claim: A related device called muḍāraʿa is illustrated by two verses from al-Khansāʾ.
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r3.anchor: ومما يقارب الترصيع ضرب يسمى المضارعة وذلك كقول الخنساء

BAQILLANI:v1p96/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r4.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r4.claim: Takāfuʾ is close to antithesis; examples include sayings attributed to al-Manṣūr, ʿUmar ibn Dharr, Bashshār, and unnamed Arabs.
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r4.anchor: ومن البديع باب التكافؤ وذلك قريب من المطابقة كقول المنصور لا تخرجوا من عز الطاعة إلى ذل المعصية

BAQILLANI:v1p96/r5.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r5.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r5.claim: He names taʿaṭṭuf as another rhetorical device and illustrates it with a line by Imruʾ al-Qays.
BAQILLANI:v1p96/r5.anchor: عود على عود على عود خلق

BURHAN:v1p73/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p73/r1.claim: Qur'anic verse endings use either identical letters or letters close in sound; examples include the matched moon and two nearly matched Fatiha endings.
BURHAN:v1p73/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى ﴿ اقتربت الساعة وانشق القمر ﴾ وجميع هذه السورة على الازدواج

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r7.claim: God removes the Prophet's distress at the enemies' accusation of madness by emphatically denying it; God answers and refutes what enemies say about His Messenger.
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r7.anchor: ما أوجب لصدره من الوحشة من قول الأعداء عنه : إنه مجنون ، أزاله عنه بنفيه

ITQAN:v2p500/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p500/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p500/r11.claim: Another view makes lā deny the preceding rejection of resurrection, after which the oath begins; the Qur’an can place a statement and its answer in different sūras.
ITQAN:v2p500/r11.anchor: وقيل نافية لما تقدم عندهم من إنكار البعث فقيل لهم ليس الأمر كذلك ثم استؤنف القسم

ITQAN:v3p296/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p296/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p296/r4.claim: Surat Nun begins by denying that the Prophet is mad by his Lord's grace and closes with the disbelievers' accusation that he is mad.

ITQAN:v3p279/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p279/r1.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
ITQAN:v3p279/r1.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isba‘ calls تشريع التوأم: a poem is built on two meters, and dropping one or two feet leaves a complete line in another meter.
ITQAN:v3p279/r1.anchor: أحدهما التشريع سماه ابن أبي الأصبع التوأم وأصله أن يبني الشاعر بيته على وزنين من أوزان العروض

ITQAN:v3p279/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p279/r2.speaker: آخرون
ITQAN:v3p279/r2.claim: Other theorists extend تشريع to prose: a second rhymed clause can follow a complete, informative first clause, adding meaning without reducing completeness.
ITQAN:v3p279/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون بل يكون في النثر بأن يبنى على سجعتين لو اقتصر على الأولى منهما كان الكلام تاما مفيدا

ITQAN:v3p279/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p279/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p279/r5.claim: الالتزام, or لزوم ما لا يلزم, is the unforced commitment to one or more letters before the rhyme; the two verses about the Prophet and his reward commit to two letters.
ITQAN:v3p279/r5.anchor: الثاني الالتزام ويسمى لزوم ما لا يلزم وهو أن يلتزم في الشعر أو النثر حرف أو حرفان فصاعدا قبل الروي

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r1.speaker: ابن جريج
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jurayj says people called the Prophet mad and then a devil, prompting the assurance that he was not mad by his Lord’s favor.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال كانوا يقولون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه مجنون ثم شيطان فنزلت

NAHHAS:v5p5/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p5/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p5/r1.claim: God's gift of intellect and understanding, and the Prophet's being the wisest of his time, refute the charge that he is mad.
NAHHAS:v5p5/r1.anchor: أي ما أنت بما أنعم الله عليك من العقل والفهم إذا كان أعقل أهل زمانه بمجنون

NAHHAS:v5p5/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p5/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p5/r2.claim: Majnūn means one whose mind is covered; the root also describes night covering, a fetus, a grave, and a shield.
NAHHAS:v5p5/r2.anchor: وهو المستور العقل ومن هذا جن عليه الليل وأجنه ومنه قيل جنين وللقبر جنن

NAHHAS:v5p5/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p5/r3.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
NAHHAS:v5p5/r3.claim: ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa's poem uses مجني for a shield, illustrating the sense of covering.
NAHHAS:v5p5/r3.anchor: قال عمر بن أبي ربيعة ( وكان مجني دون من كنت أتقي

NAHHAS:v5p5/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p5/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p5/r4.claim: Arab usage has أجن فهو مجنون, though the regular form would be مجن.
NAHHAS:v5p5/r4.anchor: مسموع من العرب على غير قياس أجن فهو مجنون والقياس مجن

NAHHAS:v5p5/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p5/r5.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v5p5/r5.claim: Al-Mubarrad preferred the regular derivation from جن.
NAHHAS:v5p5/r5.anchor: وحكى لنا علي بن سليمان عن محمد بن يزيد أنه كان يذهب إلى القياس في هذا

SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r1.claim: The author points to the similar phrase in 52:29 for an earlier detailed discussion.
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r1.anchor: قد تقدم نظير هذا في الطور في قوله

SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attaches بنعمة to مجنون despite negation; he calls it circumstantial and treats ب as extra emphasis for negation.
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r2.anchor: إلا أن الزمخشري قال هنا: " فإن قلت: بم تتعلق الباء في " بنعمة ربك " وما محله؟ قلت: تتعلق بمجنون

SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r3.claim: The Shaykh says attachment needs scrutiny: negation may target only a predicate’s modifier or negate the predicate and modifier; the first reading of ما زيد قائم مسرعا denies haste only.
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r3.anchor: إذا تسلط النفي على محكوم به، وذلك له معمول، ففي ذلك طريقان، أحدهما

SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r4.claim: The Shaykh says the second scope of negation would make the parsing entail an impermissible statement about the protected Prophet.
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r4.anchor: وهذا الذي قررناه لا يتأتى معه قول الزمخشري بوجه، بل يؤدي إلى ما لا يجوز النطق به في حق المعصوم

SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r5.claim: The Shaykh instead takes بنعمة as an oath interposed between subject and predicate to strengthen the denial.
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r5.anchor: واختار الشيخ أن يكون " بنعمة " قسما معترضا به بين المحكوم عليه والحكم

SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls بنعمة ربك an aside like أنت بحمد الله فاضل, but does not explain what governs ب.
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " بنعمة ربك " اعتراض كما تقول للإنسان: " أنت بحمد الله فاضل

SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r7.claim: The author says ب attaches to the conveyed sentence meaning with causal force; in the example it attaches directly to فاضل.
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r7.anchor: قلت: والذي تتعلق به الباء في هذا النحو معنى مضمون الجملة نفيا وإثباتا، كأنه قيل: انتفى عنك ذلك بحمد الله

SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r8.speaker: صاحب المنتخب
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r8.claim: The al-Muntakhab glosses the meaning as God’s favor having kept madness away from the Prophet.
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r8.anchor: وقد نحا صاحب " المنتخب " إلى هذا فقال: " المعنى: انتفى عنك الجنون بنعمة ربك

SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r9.claim: Another interpretation separates بنعمة ربك and reads it as and the favor belongs to your Lord, like سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك meaning praise belongs to God.
SAMIN-DURR:68:2/r9.anchor: وقيل: معناه: ما أنت بمجنون، والنعمة لربك، كقولهم:

SAMIN-DURR:68:2#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:68:2#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:68:2#2/r1.claim: The author cites Labīd’s جار بأربد نافع as meaning and Arbīd is helpful; he says the line illustrates meaning, not parsing.
SAMIN-DURR:68:2#2/r1.anchor: أي: وهو أربد ". وهذا ليس بتفسير إعراب بل تفسير معنى

ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r2.claim: In the construction with mā, anta is its subject and bi-majnūn its predicate; bi-niʿmati rabbika is attached to the negation.

ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r3.claim: The sense is that, by your Lord's grace, madness is absent from you, just as one may say that God's blessing made someone understanding rather than ignorant.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r3.anchor: المعنى: انتفى عنك الجنون بنعمة ربك، كما تقول: أنت بنعمة الله فهم

ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r4.claim: This denial answers the opponents' claim that the recipient of the Reminder was mad.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r4.anchor: وهذا جواب لقولهم: (وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر

ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n3/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n3/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n3/r1.claim: The claim that Muhammad was mad recalls the taunt used by most contemporaries from the start of his preaching and continued for years.
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n3/r1.anchor: This is an allusion to the taunt with which most of Muhammad's contemporaries greeted the beginning of his preaching

ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n3/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n3/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n3/r2.claim: More broadly, the passage applies to all followers who base moral judgments on belief in God and the afterlife.
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n3/r2.anchor: not merely to the Prophet but also to all who followed or will follow him: in this particular instance, to all who base their moral valuations on their belief in God and in life after death

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p281/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p281/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p281/r1.claim: The reassurance that Muhammad is not mad answers the accusation in al-Hijr that called him mad because the Reminder had been sent down to him.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p281/r1.anchor: رداً على ما في سورة أخرى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.claim: The opening verses affirm the Prophet’s mission and steady him against deniers who dispute the miracle and claim the Qur’an is merely tales of the ancients.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.anchor: واضح أن الآيات موجهه إلى تأييد نبوة المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، تثبيت قلبه في مواجهة من يكذبونه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r2.claim: At the beginning of revelation, Quraysh’s leaders called the Prophet mad after he urged them to abandon the idols their fathers worshipped.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r2.anchor: وقد وصفوه بالجنون حين دعاهم إلى ترك أوثانهم التي وجدوا آباءهم لها عابدين

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r5.claim: The author dates the dispute over the miracle to the earliest mission, when only the first verses of al-ʿAlaq had been revealed; nūn then signals the secret of the Qur’an’s miraculous expression.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r5.anchor: ولم يكن قد نزل من القرآن غير الآيات الأولى من سورة العلق. ومجئ الحرف (ن) في سورة القلم المكية المبكرة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r1.claim: Grammarians and exegetes treat the bāʾ before the predicate of mā as extra, like bāʾ with laysa: it governs the surface genitive while the underlying predicate remains accusative.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r1.anchor: جرى النحاة والمفسرون على القول بأن هذه الباء زائدة في خبر ما، كما تأتي زائدة في خبر ليس

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r2.claim: “Extra” does not mean pointless: Ibn Hishām classifies this bāʾ with other added bāʾs as conveying emphasis.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r2.anchor: لا يعنون بلفظ الزيادة أنها تأتي عبثاً أو لغواً، وإنما هي زائدة عندهم للتأكيد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r3.claim: Although grammarians recognize that added bāʾ can be obligatory or common in some constructions, they assign its effect to wording rather than meaning.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r3.anchor: جرت الصنعة الإعرابية على قصر عملها على اللفظ دون المعنى

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r4.claim: Her Qur’anic survey finds this bāʾ frequent with explicit, non-interpreted singular predicates after mā and laysa.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p181/r4.anchor: ظاهرة مجيء هذه الباء المقول بزيادتها، في خبرهما المفرد الصريح غير المؤول

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p282/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p282/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p282/r4.claim: The author rejects treating lā in oath formulas as a reply to earlier speech: the readings join lā to uqsimu, and al-Qalam’s denial cannot answer al-Ḥijr’s accusation because al-Qalam was revealed far earlier.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p282/r4.anchor: كل القراءات فيها على الوصل. وتنظيرهم بقوله تعالى: {مَا أَنْتَ بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ بِمَجْنُونٍ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r1.claim: Al-Tur names several accusations, including soothsayer, madman, poet and fabricator; al-Qalam mentions only madness, so the extra denial of soothsaying suits al-Tur.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r1.anchor: فقد ذكروا أنه كاهن، وذكروا أنه مجنون، وذكروا أنه شاعر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r2.claim: Al-Tur's claim that listeners should bring clear authority from their hearing evokes the jinn-listening claimed by soothsayers, making the added word كاهن apt.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r2.anchor: والاستماع مما تدعيه الكهنة لتابعيهم من الجن

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r3.claim: Because al-Tur also challenges the audience over magic, denying that the Prophet is a soothsayer fits that surah's subject matter.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r4.claim: Al-Tur opens with a much longer oath than al-Qalam, whose oath is only by the pen and what is written; this broader setting suits the added accusation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p168/r4.anchor: توسع في القسم في أول سورة الطور بخلاف سورة القلم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r1.claim: The extended opening oath in al-Tur makes its added denial of soothsaying fitting, unlike al-Qalam's brief oath by the pen and writing.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r1.anchor: فناسب التوسع في الطور هذه الزيادة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r2.claim: Al-Qalam ends by reporting the unbelievers' charge that the Prophet is mad, and its opening answers that same charge with a denial.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r2.anchor: فرد عليهم في أول السورة بنفي الجنون عنه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r3.claim: The emphatic bāʾ strengthens the negation of madness at the opening, matching the emphatic lām in the closing affirmation that they call him mad.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p169/r3.anchor: كيف ناسب التأكيد بالباء الزائدة في النفي (بمجنون) التوكيد باللام في الإثبات (لمجنون)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r3.claim: Al-Ṭūr adds kāhin because disbelievers broadened their accusations against the Prophet; its references to seers and magic also suit that addition, unlike al-Qalam’s briefer wording.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p806/r3.anchor: توسّع الكافرون في التُّهم لذا استدعى السياق إدخال كلمة (كاهن) كزيادة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r1.claim: Al-Tur adds the accusation of soothsaying because it also reports accusations of madness, poetry, and fabrication; al-Qalam names madness alone.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r1.anchor: ذكروا أنه كاهن، وذكروا أنه مجنون، وذكروا أنه شاعر.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r5.claim: Al-Qalam's opening denial of madness answers the closing charge that the Prophet is mad, making the end correspond to the beginning.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r5.anchor: فرد عليهم في أول السورة بنفي الجنون عنه فقال: (ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون) . فناسب آخر السورة أولها.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r6.claim: The emphatic ba reinforces negation in bi-majnun, while the emphatic lam reinforces the disbelievers' positive assertion la-majnun.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p109/r6.anchor: الباء لتوكيد النفي واللام لتوكيد الإثبات

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p807/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p807/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p807/r1.claim: The extra ba in al-Qalam's opening denial matches the closing accusation of madness, since the disbelievers add no charge beyond what the opening refutes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p807/r1.anchor: فزيادة الباء (بمجنون) لأنه لم يزد الكافرون عما جاء في الآيات فناسب أول السورة ما جاء في آخرها.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p807/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p807/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p807/r2.claim: Ba emphasizes a negation, whereas lam emphasizes an affirmation; inn with lam intensifies the disbelievers' assertion about the Prophet.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p807/r2.anchor: والباء تأتي لتوكيد النفي (بمجنون) واللام لتوكيد الإيجاب (لمجنون) فهو نفي مقابل للام التوكيد.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r1.claim: This is the answer to the oath: the second ب is extra for emphasis, مجنون is the predicate of ما, and the first ب marks association; its phrase is a circumstantial qualifier of the pronoun in the predicate, governed by the negation’s meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r1.anchor: جواب القسم والباء الثانية مزيدة لتأكيد النفي ومجنون خبر ما والباء الأولى للملابسة والجار والمجرور في موضع الحال من الضمير في الخبر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r2.speaker: ناصر الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r2.claim: The favored sense is that madness is absent from the Prophet while he is endowed with his Lord’s favor, including sound judgment, prophethood, and courage.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى انتفى عنك الجنون في حال كونك ملتبسا بنعمة ربك منعما عليك بما أنعم من حصافة الرأي والنبوة والشهامة واختاره ناصر الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r3.speaker: ناصر الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r3.claim: A nearby parse makes ب causal and attaches the phrase to the negation as an adverb: madness is absent because of the favor bestowed by God.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r3.anchor: وقريب منه جعل الباء للسببية والجار والمجرور متعلقا بالنفي كالظرف اللغو كأنه قيل انتفى عنك الجنون بسبب نعمة ربك عليك

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r4.speaker: ناصر الدين
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r4.claim: If the first phrase is a circumstantial qualifier governed by مجنون, it only denies madness during the favor, not at all times; Naṣir al-Din raises this semantic objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r4.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الباء للملابسة في موضع الحال والعامل مجنون وباؤه لا تمنع العمل لأنها مزيدة وتعقبه ناصر الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r5.claim: The reply that God’s favor is constant would rescue either parse, but al-Alusi distinguishes them: with مجنون as governor the wording implies madness could occur in that state, whereas the preferred parse does not restrict the negation that way.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r5.anchor: وأجيب بأن تلك الحالة لازمة له صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم غير منفكة عنه فنفيه عنه فيها مستلزم لنفيه عنه دائما وسائر الحالات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r6.claim: If the ب is causal and the phrase is an adverbial, attaching it to what follows is semantically disallowed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#2/r6.anchor: وقيل إذا حمل الباء على السببية واعتبر الظرف لغوا يظهر عدم جواز تعلقه بما بعده من حيث المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r1.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r1.claim: Al-Khafaji discusses circumstantial clauses after negation; the construction negates the state’s concurrence with its subject, not the state itself, illustrated by the cited line about a campfire appearing at night.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r1.anchor: ( ظهور نار القرى ليلا على علم ) ولهم في الجملة الحالية والحال إذا وقعت بعد النفي كلام ذكره الخفاجي

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r2.claim: Another parse makes بنعمة ربك an intervening oath, with no stated answer or one inferred from the surrounding words; Abu Hayyan prefers this analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r2.anchor: وجوز كون بنعمة ربك قسما متوسطا في الكلام لتأكيده من غير تقدير جواب أو يقدر له جواب يدل عليه الكلام المذكور واستظهر هذا الوجه أبو حيان

ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r3.claim: Calling God the Prophet’s Lord honors him and signals that God will complete His favor and raise him to unsurpassed heights; the verse clears him of the charge of madness, which his enemies made from envy and hostility.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p24#3/r3.anchor: والتعرض لوصف الربوبية المنبئة عن التبليغ إلى معارج الكمال مع الإضافة إلى ضميره عليه الصلاة والسلام لتشريفه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r1.claim: This answers the accusation in 15:6 that the Prophet was mad; God swears by Nūn, the Pen, and the written record of deeds.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r1.anchor: {ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون} [هو] (3) جواب لقولهم "يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون" (الحجر-6) فأقسم الله بالنون والقلم وما يكتب من الأعمال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r2.claim: Here the Lord's niʿma means the prophethood with which God blessed the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r2.anchor: فقال: {ما أنت بنعمة ربك} بنبوة ربك

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r3.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r3.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase to mean by your Lord's protection.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r4.claim: Another parsing reads the phrase parenthetically as “and praise be to God.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو كما يقال: ما أنت بمجنون [والحمد لله] (4)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r5.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r5.claim: A further parsing means you are not mad, while the blessing belongs to your Lord, like “glory and praise be to You.”
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: معناه ما أنت بمجنون والنعمة لربك، كقولهم: سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك، أي: والحمد لك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r1.claim: This answers the oath: by God's favor in granting prophethood and sound judgment, Muḥammad is not mad.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r1.anchor: جواب القسم والمعنى ما أنت بمجنون

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r2.claim: The circumstantial phrase is governed by the meaning of negation; alternatively, the extra bāʾ in majnūn does not prevent it governing the preceding phrase, though Bayḍāwī questions that analysis semantically.

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r3.claim: Another analysis says the bāʾ in majnūn is extra and does not block its governing an earlier phrase; Bayḍāwī finds this semantically questionable.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r3.anchor: الباء لا تمنع عمله فيما قبله لأنها مزيدة

BINTSHATI:v2p40/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r1.claim: Reports that the verse concerned al-Walīd or Abū Jahl do not restrict its general wording without contextual evidence; occasions of revelation are clues to the circumstances of revelation.
BINTSHATI:v2p40/r1.anchor: وكونها نزلت في الوليد أو أبي جهل لا يقتضي الاعتبار بخصوص السبب، حيث لا قرينة تصرف إليه عموم لفظ الآية

BINTSHATI:v2p45/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r1.speaker: خديجة
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r1.claim: Hadith and sīra accounts depict Muhammad returning from the cave on Laylat al-Qadr distressed; Khadīja reassures him that God will never humiliate him, citing his virtues.
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r1.anchor: وأفضى إلى زوجه السيدة خديجة بما رأى وما سمع فقالت رضي الله عنها: أبشر يا ابن العم واثبت

BINTSHATI:v2p45/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r2.speaker: ورقة بن نوفل
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r2.claim: Waraqa ibn Nawfal tells Muhammad he is the prophet of this community and will be called a liar, harmed, fought, and expelled.
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r2.anchor: "ورقة بن نوفل" لخبر الوحي الأول، وقوله للمصطفى عليه

BINTSHATI:v2p45/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r3.claim: These assurances fortify the Prophet at the beginning of revelation, prepare him for the burden of conveying the message, and sustain him through the abuse of deniers.
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r3.anchor: فندرك عمق أثرها في تثبيت المصطفى وتقوية فؤاده، وتهيئته لما هو بسيل أن يحتمل من أعباء التبليغ

BINTSHATI:v2p45/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r4.claim: Most exegetes treat “by your Lord's grace” as parenthetical, like saying, “By God's favor, you are virtuous”; Bint al-Shati prefers this simple parsing.
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r4.anchor: وجمهرة المفسرين على أن جملة {بنعمة ربك} اعتراضية، كما تقول لصاحبك: أنت بحمد الله فاضل.

BINTSHATI:v2p45/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān offers the alternative sense “you are not mad, by your Lord's blessing”; Bint al-Shati rejects it as a meaning-only gloss rather than a syntactic parsing.
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r5.anchor: ذكره "أبو حيان" في (البحر) وقال إنه تفسير معنى لا تفسير إعراب.

BINTSHATI:v2p45/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r6.claim: Bint al-Shati considers Abū Ḥayyān's construal strained and prefers ordinary Arabic phrasing, like “by God's favor, you are not wretched.”
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r6.anchor: وفيه تكلف لا يسيغه حس العربية المرهف الذي يجلوه البيان القرآني

BINTSHATI:v2p45/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r7.claim: Her earlier survey in al-Takāthur found that the Qur'an uses niʿma for worldly blessings and reserves the form naʿīm for the bliss of the afterlife.
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r7.anchor: وقد سبق استقراء ما في القرآن من لفظ نعمة، مادة وصيغة،

BINTSHATI:v2p46/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r1.claim: Grammarians treat the bāʾ before majnūn as extra: it governs the word's genitive form while its syntactic position remains nominative, hidden by the preposition's kasra.
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r1.anchor: فهي تعمل في لفظ الخبر، ويبقى الحكم الإعرابي على أصله، يمنع من ظهور حركته

BINTSHATI:v2p46/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r2.claim: Across the Qur'an, this bāʾ regularly occurs in the single-word predicate of mā and laysa, with only a few context-specific exceptions.
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r2.anchor: وباستقراء ما في القرآن الكريم من خبر ليس وما، يلقانا اطراد وقوع هذه الباء المقول بزيادتها

BINTSHATI:v2p46/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r3.claim: Bint al-Shati objects to calling the bāʾ extra, since that would imply it could be removed, a possibility the Qur'anic style does not support.
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r3.anchor: ولا يهون القول بأن الباء حرف جر زائد، إذ مقتضى القول بزيادتها إمكان الاستغناء عنها

BINTSHATI:v2p46/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r4.speaker: النحويون من المفسرين
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r4.claim: Grammatical exegetes say the bāʾ is added to intensify the negation; Bint al-Shati instead says it makes the denial categorical.
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r4.anchor: والنحويون من المفسرين، يذهبون إلى أن الباء زائدة لتأكيد النفي

BINTSHATI:v2p46/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r5.claim: In negative mā or laysa clauses, the bāʾ makes the statement a categorical denial; in interrogative negatives it turns the statement into an insistent affirmation, and the particle consistently remains on the predicate.
BINTSHATI:v2p46/r5.anchor: هو أن الباء تأتي في خبر المنفي بما أو ليس، فتجعله جحداً وإنكاراً

BINTSHATI:v2p47/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p47/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p47/r1.claim: In this verse the bāʾ after mā makes the denial that the Prophet is mad categorical.
BINTSHATI:v2p47/r1.anchor: وفي آية القلم، تأتي الباء في خبر المنفي بما، فتصير به إلى إنكار بات

BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.claim: The sūra’s closing words support the Prophet and link back to its opening, which likewise affirms his freedom from madness and his great character.
BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.anchor: تأييداً للمصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، يرتبط بما بدأت به السورة من مثل هذا التأييد الإلهي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r9.claim: As a lead-in to the denial of madness, the author recalls that the Prophet had lived among his audience for forty years, was their most virtuous and wise, and was known as the trustworthy one.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p94#2/r9.anchor: قد عاشر المرسل إليهم دهرا طويلا وزمنا مديدا أربعين سنة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r1.claim: After the great oath, God comforts the Prophet and refutes the accusation of madness, which arose only after the unmatched blessing bestowed on him.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r1.anchor: قال مجيبا هذا القسم العظيم رادا عليهم بأجلى ما يكون وأدله على المراد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r2.claim: The blessing is God’s nurturing of the Prophet’s lofty aspirations and complete dispositions, and His choosing him for the Quran, which gathers all knowledge and wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r2.anchor: أي بسبب إنعام { ربك } المربي لك

BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r3.claim: The intensified denial honors the Prophet; the person who calls him mad deserves that name, and the accusation exceeds the earlier charge of misguidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r3.anchor: وأكد النفي زيادة في شرفه صل الله عليه وسلم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r4.claim: Al-Mulk had left open which of the Prophet and his opponents was plainly astray; evidence in its signs establishes their error and his guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r4.anchor: فستعلمون من هو في ضلال مبين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r5.claim: The denial removes misery caused by defective reason and confirms happiness grounded in sound reason and God’s favor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r5.anchor: فنفى عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم الشقاوة التي سببها فساد العقل

BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr says al-Mulk contains proofs so immense that minds cannot exhaust them, including reflection on the creation of the seven heavens; no grading applies.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r6.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما تضمنت سورة الملك من عظيم البراهين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r7.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r7.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr glosses ṭibāqan as one layer matching another, deriving it from layering a sandal sole; he says this suggests equal dimensions and exact matching without excess or deficiency.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p95/r7.anchor: أي يطابق بعضها بعضا من طابق النعل - إذا خصفها طبقا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r1.claim: The proofs developed in al-Mulk, which surpass ordinary rational insight, could not issue from someone insane; the accusations of madness, sorcery, poetry, and lying are false.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r1.anchor: فأنى يصدر بعض عن متصف ببعض ما هزئوا به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r2.claim: The Qur’an’s concise, miraculous order and harmony are beyond human minds; the challenge says humans and jinn cannot produce its like.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r2.anchor: قد انقطعت دونها أنظار العقلاء فكيف ببسطها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r3.claim: This verse answers the opponents’ closing claim that Muhammad is mad, recorded at the end of the sūra.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r3.anchor: جوابا لقوله تعالى في آخر السورة إنه لمجنون

BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.claim: Biqāʿī says denial precedes the quoted accusation to honor the Prophet and soften its impact; placing praise of his character before the accusation heightens that honor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.anchor: وتقدم الجواب بنفي قولهم والتنزيه عنه على حكاية قولهم ليكون أبلغ في إجلاله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r5.claim: The Qur’an’s freedom from contradiction is another proof supporting the Prophet’s truth and this denial.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r5.anchor: ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

DURR-FULL:v8p242/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the verse was revealed after people called the Prophet mad and claimed a demon possessed him.
DURR-FULL:v8p242/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال: كانوا يقولون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنه لمجنون به شيطان فنزلت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r1.claim: Denying madness establishes the very thing the polytheists meant to deny: the Prophet’s messengership, since they substituted madness for the claim of being a messenger.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r1.anchor: والمقصود من نفي الجنون عنه إثبات ما قصد المشركون نفيه وهو أن يكون رسولا من الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r2.claim: The response outmatches the polytheists’ assertion in 68:51 with three reinforcements: an oath, the emphatic ب after negation, and a negative nominal sentence whose form signals an established fact.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r2.anchor: بمؤكدات أقوى مما في كلامهم إذ أقسم عليه وجيء بعد النفي بالباء التي تزاد بعد النفي لتأكيده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī construes بنعمة ربك as a circumstantial phrase attached to the pronoun in مجنون: the madness is absent through God’s favor, with ب indicating accompaniment or cause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r3.anchor: جعله في ( الكشاف ) حالا من الضمير الذي في مجنون المنفي . والتقدير : انتفى وصف المجنون بنعمة ربك عليك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r4.speaker: ابن الحاجب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r4.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib attaches the phrase to the verbal meaning implicit in ما, estimating that madness is negated by God’s favor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r4.anchor: وذهب ابن الحاجب في ( أماليه ) أن { بنعمة ربك } متعلق بما يتضمنه حرف { ما } النافية من معنى الفعل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r5.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r5.claim: Ibn Hishām favors Ibn al-Ḥājib’s analysis in مغني اللبيب, but it conflicts with grammarians’ consensus against attaching an adverbial to a particle, apart from narrow allowances by Abū ʿAlī and Abū al-Fatḥ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r5.anchor: واستحسن هذا ابن هشام في ( مغني اللبيب ) في الباب الثالث لولا أنه مخالف لاتفاق النحاة على عدم صحة تعلق الظرف بالحرف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r6.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers a parenthetical clause with ب attached to an omitted predicate, تقديره أن ذلك بنعمة ربك, matching Arabic usage and the construction in 11:41.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r6.anchor: والذي أرى أن تكون جملة معترضة وأن الباء متعلقة بمحذوف يدل عليه المقام وتقديره : أن ذلك بنعمة ربك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r7.speaker: الفضل بن عباس اللهبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r7.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr cites the poet al-Faḍl ibn ʿAbbās al-Lāhibī’s usage of بنعمة الله as evidence for attaching the phrase to an omitted clause.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r7.anchor: كقول الحماسي الفضل بن عباس اللهبي : كل له نية في بغض صاحبه بنعمة الله نقليكم وتقلونا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r8.claim: The discussion has a parallel in the earlier phrase فما أنت بنعمة ربك بكاهن ولا مجنون.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p61/r8.anchor: وتقدم نظيره في قوله : { فما أنت بنعمة ربك بكاهن ولا مجنون في سورة الطور .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r1.claim: Though exegetes did not usually treat jurisprudential theory as tafsir material, rulings on commands, prohibitions, and general wording are used; usul al-fiqh contributes in two ways.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r1.anchor: أحكام الأوامر والنواهي والعموم وهي من أصول الفقه ، فتحصل أن بعضه يكون مادة للتفسير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r2.claim: First, usul al-fiqh explains Arabic interpretive methods often omitted by grammarians, such as implication and the contrary implication; al-Ghazali also counts it among Qur’anic and legal sciences.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r2.anchor: قد أودعت فيه مسائل كثيرة هي من طرق استعمال كلام العرب وفهم موارد اللغة أهمل التنبيه عليها علماء العربية مثل مسائل الفحوى ومفهوم المخالفة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r3.claim: Second, usul al-fiqh systematizes inference rules and equips the exegete to derive legal meanings from Qur’anic verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r3.anchor: أن علم الأصول يضبط قواعد الاستنباط ويفصح عنها فهو آلة للمفسر في استنباط المعاني الشرعية من آياتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r4.speaker: عبد الحكيم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r4.claim: Abd al-Hakim counts kalam as a prerequisite because tafsir presupposes establishing that God speaks.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r4.anchor: على إثبات كونه تعالى متكلما ، وذلك يحتاج إلى علم الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r5.speaker: الآلوسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r5.claim: Al-Alusi says kalam is needed to know what may or may not be ascribed to God, especially in ambiguous attribute verses such as “The Merciful sat upon the Throne”; Ibn Ashur says this is closer than Abd al-Hakim’s rationale and derives from al-Jurjani.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r5.anchor: وقال الآلوسي لتوقف فهم ما يجوز على الله ويستحيل على الكلام يعني من آيات التشابه في الصفات مثل الرحمن على العرش استوى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects both arguments: God’s speech was established before kalam and is not a tafsir prerequisite; knowledge of divine possibility likewise needs kalam only for extended argument, and an advanced need does not make a discipline tafsir material.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r6.anchor: وكلاهما اشتباه لأن كون القرآن كلام الله قد تقرر عند سلف الأمة قبل علم الكلام ، ولا أثر له في التفسير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r7.claim: Unlike al-Suyuti, Ibn Ashur does not count jurisprudence itself as a tafsir source: understanding the Qur’an does not depend on fiqh, which is later than and derived from tafsir.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r7.anchor: ولم نعد الفقه من مادة علم التفسير كما فعل السيوطي ، لعدم توقف فهم القرآن ، على مسائل الفقه ، فإن علم الفقه متأخر عن التفسير وفرع عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r8.claim: Fiqh helps expand exegesis through detailed inference, legal meanings, etiquette, and other fields; al-Baydawi says only someone learned in all religious sciences and Arabic and literary disciplines should undertake it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r8.anchor: لا يكاد يحصر ما يحتاجه المتبحر في ذلك من العلوم ، ويوشك أن يكون المفسر المتوسع محتاجا إلى الإلمام بكل العلوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r9.claim: Prophetic and Companion reports explaining verses are themselves tafsir, not external disciplines from which tafsir derives.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r9.anchor: لا يعد من استمداد علم التفسير ، الآثار المروية عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في تفسير آيات ، ولا ما يروى عن الصحابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r10.claim: A Qur’anic passage explaining another is also internal exegesis, including specification of general wording, qualification of the unrestricted, clarification of the ambiguous, and implications of wording.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r10.anchor: ولا يعد أيضا من استمداد التفسير ما في بعض آي القرآن من معنى يفسر بعضا آخر منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r11.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r11.claim: Ibn Hisham quotes Abu Ali al-Farisi that the Qur’an is like one sura: an accusation that the recipient of the Reminder is mad is answered elsewhere by the assurance that the Prophet is not mad by his Lord’s grace.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r11.anchor: ذكر ابن هشام ، في مغنى اللبيب ، في حرف لا ، عن أبي علي الفارسي ، أن القرآن كله كالسورة الواحدة ، ولهذا يذكر الشيء في سورة وجوابه في سورة أخرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r12.claim: Ibn Ashur says it is too broad to call the entire Qur’an one sura: some verses interpret others, but some stand independently, and a meaning in one passage need not apply to analogous passages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r12.anchor: وهذا كلام لا يحسن إطلاقه ، لأن القرآن قد يحمل بعض آياته على بعض وقد يستقل بعضها عن بعض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r13.claim: Tafsir remains a principal Islamic science in general even when it borrows other sciences for fuller detail; its status as a root and its detailed dependence on them operate in different respects, as Abd al-Hakim explains.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p25/r13.anchor: فأما استمداده من بعض العلوم الإسلامية ، فذلك استمداد لقصد تفصيل التفسير على وجه أتم من الإجمال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r5.claim: If ن means the fish, the pen is what God created and commanded to record events, and “they write” refers to angels.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r5.anchor: فمن قال إنه اسم الحوت جعل «القلم» الذي خلقه الله تعالى وأمره فكتب الكائنات وجعل الضمير في يسطرون للملائكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r6.claim: If ن means an inkpot, the pen is the familiar human pen and “they write” refers to people, as Ibn ʿAbbās states.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p345#2/r6.anchor: ومن قال بأن «نون» اسم للدواة، جعل «القلم» هذا المتعارف بأيدي الناس. نص ذلك ابن عباس وجعل الضمير في يسطرون للناس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r8.claim: This is the oath's answer; ما operates with a subject and predicate, as when باء enters the predicate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r8.anchor: وقوله: ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمجنون هو جواب القسم وما هنا عاملة لها اسم وخبر، وكذلك هي حيث دخلت الباء في الخبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r9.claim: بنعمة ربك is parenthetical, as in “you are, praise be to God, virtuous.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r9.anchor: وقوله: بنعمة ربك اعتراض، كما يقول الإنسان: أنت بحمد الله فاضل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r10.claim: Quraysh accused the Prophet of insanity, implying his speech was wrong like a madman's; God denied and honored him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p346/r10.anchor: وسبب هذه الآية، أن قريشا رمت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالجنون، وهو ستر العقول، بمعنى أن كلامه خطأ ككلام المجنون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p328/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p328/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p328/r1.claim: By the blessing of his Lord, meaning God's gift of faith and prophethood, the Prophet is not mad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p328/r1.anchor: أي ما أنت بإنعام ربك عليكم بالإيمان والنبوة بمجنون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p328/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p328/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p328/r2.claim: The verse answers their claim that the Prophet was mad: by God's favor, madness has departed from him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p328/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج هذا جواب قولهم إنك لمجنون وتأويله فارقك الجنون بنعمة الله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r3.claim: The Prophet is not mad, despite the ignorant people among his nation who denied the guidance and manifest truth he brought and called him mad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p187#2/r3.anchor: أي: لست، ولله الحمد، بمجنون، كما قد يقوله الجهلة من قومك،

JISHUMI:v10p7021/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7021/r8.claim: Junūn means loss of reason and derives from concealment.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r1.claim: The preposition ب attaches to the negated مجنون just as it attaches to عاقل in an affirmative sentence; negation does not change the verb's operation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r1.anchor: يتعلق بمجنون منفيا ، كما يتعلق بعاقل مثبتا في قولك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r2.claim: The phrase is in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase: ‘not insane, while blessed by your Lord.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r2.anchor: ومحله النصب على الحال ، كأنه قال : ما أنت بمجنون منعما عليك بذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r3.claim: The extra ب reinforces the negation and does not prevent مجنون from governing what precedes it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r3.anchor: ولم تمنع الباء أن يعمل مجنون فيما قبله ، لأنها زائدة لتأكيد النفي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r4.claim: The verse repudiates the Meccan disbelievers' accusation, arising from enmity and envy, and points to God's gift of sound judgment and courage fitting for prophethood.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p589#2/r4.anchor: استبعاد ما كان ينسبه إليه كفار مكة عداوة وحسدا ، وأنه من إنعام الله عليه بحصافة العقل والشهامة

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r16.claim: The polytheists claimed the Prophet was mad and possessed by a demon; the verse refutes them, and 15:6 preserves their taunt.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r16.anchor: كان المشركون يقولون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه مجنون به شيطان , وهو قولهم : ^ { يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر إنك لمجنون } ^ [ الحجر : 6 ]

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r17.anchor: أي برحمة ربك , والنعمة ها هنا الرحمة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r18.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r18.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is an oath: by your Lord's blessing, you are not mad, since both waw and ba can mark an oath.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r18.anchor: ويحتمل ثانيا : أن النعمة ها هنا قسم , وتقديره : ما أنت ونعمة ربك بمجنون , لأن الواو والباء من حروف القسم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r19.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r19.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets the phrase non-literally as saying the Prophet is not unsuccessful.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p59/r19.anchor: وتأوله الكلبي على غير ظاهره , فقال : معناه ما أنت بنعمة ربك بمخفق .

MUQATIL:68:2-4/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:68:2-4/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:68:2-4/r1.claim: God's favor means His mercy, and Muhammad is not insane.
MUQATIL:68:2-4/r1.anchor: { مآ أنت } يا محمد { بنعمة ربك } يعني برحمة ربك { بمجنون }

NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r1.claim: The blessing is God's favor to the Prophet, including prophethood and other gifts; the verse denies that he is mad.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r1.anchor: أي بانعامه عليك بالنبوة وغيرها فأنت اسم وما وخبرها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r2.claim: “أنت” is the subject of “ما” and “بمجنون” its predicate; “بنعمة ربك” interrupts them as a circumstantial phrase attached to an omitted expression, with an accusative position governed by “بمجنون”.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r2.anchor: وبنعمة ربك اعتراض بين الاسم والخبر والباء في بنعمة ربك تتعلق بمحذوف ومحله النصب على الحال

NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r3.claim: The extra bāʾ strengthens the negation and does not prevent “مجنون” from governing what precedes it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r3.anchor: ولم تمنع الباء أن يعمل مجنون فيما قبله لأنها زائدة لتأكيد النفي

NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r4.claim: The denial answers the opponents' accusation that the recipient of the Reminder was mad.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p268/r4.anchor: وهو جواب قولهم وقالوا يا أيها الذي نزل عليه الذكر انك لمجنون

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r10.claim: This is the oath's answer, refuting the polytheists' claim that the Prophet was insane and possessed by a devil; compare 15:6.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r10.anchor: هذا جواب القسم وهو نفي وكان المشركون يقولون للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنه مجنون، به شيطان.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r11.anchor: أي برحمة ربك. والنعمة ههنا الرحمة.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r12.claim: Alternatively, the phrase is an oath: “By your Lord's favor, you are not mad,” since both wāw and bāʾ can mark an oath.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r12.anchor: ويحتمل ثانيا أن النعمة ههنا قسم وتقديره: ما أنت ونعمة ربك بمجنون

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r13.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r13.claim: Another analysis reads the statement as “You are not mad, and praise belongs to God.”
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r13.anchor: وقيل هو كما تقول: ما أنت بمجنون، والحمد لله.

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r14.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r14.claim: A further analysis takes it to mean “You are not mad, and the favor belongs to your Lord,” like the expression “Glory and praise be to You, O God.”
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r14.anchor: وقيل: معناه ما أنت بمجنون، والنعمة لربك كقولهم: سبحانك اللهم وبحمدك

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r15.speaker: لبيد والنابغة
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r15.claim: The quoted lines of Labīd and al-Nābigha illustrate supplying an understood “he is” in a coordinated phrase.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r15.anchor:
ومنه قول لبيد:
وأفردت في الدنيا بفقد عشيرتي
وفارقني جار بأربد نافع
أي وهو أربد. وقال النابغة:

QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r16.claim: The prepositional phrase attaches to the negated “mad,” as it would to an affirmed predicate; its accusative role is circumstantial, meaning he is not mad while favored by God.
QURTUBI-FULL:68:1-3/r16.anchor: والباء في { بنعمة ربك } متعلقة { بمجنون } منفيا كما يتعلق بغافل مثبتا.
